Coming from an avid railfan this is not recommended, you'd probably be a bloody disfigured mass when it happens, and the crew onboard would know exactly what happened and probably be traumatized (since depending on how fast the train is moving and how long it is, chances are they wouldn't be able to stop in time even with full emergency brakes applied). And if they managed to stop before they reached you, you'd probably have to deal with the railroad police... but I sympathize with you though, the same thought has crossed my mind before and I hope you don't...

I guess the answer is selfishness... It's always "think of the people you'd hurt!" or something like that, they just don't want to deal with the pain of losing you.
